intro_html: Chicken parm is a restaurant order that usually comes with a restaurant price. This meal-prep version skips the breading and the deep fryer but keeps everything you actually love: tender chicken, marinara, and a blanket of melty cheese over high-protein pasta. At 42 grams of protein a bowl for about $3.30 (at everyday cost), it is a filling, high-protein dinner.
cost_closing_html: About $3.30 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a chicken parm that would run $16 or more at a sit-down spot.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near 403 calories and 42 grams of protein.

shop_smart: Chicken on sale, frozen, is the move that quietly lowers the cost of half the recipes on this site.
A little parmesan goes far. One container covers several batches, so the per-serving cost stays tiny.
Store-brand sauce and cheese save a couple dollars with no difference on the plate.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Cube the chicken and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer a couple of minutes until hot.
Add the drained penne and stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top and cover for a minute until it melts.

head.description: A lightened-up chicken parmesan meal prep over high-protein penne. Fourteen servings at about 403 calories and 42 grams of protein for roughly $3.30 each (at everyday cost).

recipeIngredient: 3.5 lb raw Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast
steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Cube and cook the chicken until it reaches 165F.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer until hot.
Stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan.
Top with mozzarella and cover until melted.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.
